expect:
AO1 (12 marks): Critical, exploratory response. Must cover both bullet points: detailed analysis of the school scene, Fezziwig, and Belle in Stave 2; wider references to Marley’s regret (Stave 1), the structural purpose of looking backwards before looking forward.

AO2 (12 marks): Analyses methods — the Ghost’s light symbolism, pathetic fallacy in the decaying school, contrast between Fezziwig and Scrooge, Belle’s biblical ‘golden idol’ imagery, Scrooge’s increasing emotional language (‘wept’, ‘No more!’). Explores the structural progression from tears to shame to grief.

AO3 (6 marks): Context — Victorian boarding schools, employer-employee relations during the Industrial Revolution, the role of women (Belle has no choice but to release Scrooge from the engagement). Links to Dickens’s own childhood experiences.

Top-band responses will argue that Stave 2 is the psychological foundation for Scrooge’s redemption: change begins with self-awareness, and Dickens structures the memories to strip away Scrooge’s defences layer by layer.
